blueprint_topic: Management of Care — multidisciplinary coordination of heart-transplant candidate evaluation
stem: A nurse is preparing a client for evaluation as a heart-transplant candidate. Which explanation of the evaluation process is most accurate?

options.A: The evaluation is multidisciplinary and includes medical assessment plus psychosocial factors such as support, adherence, substance use, and mental health.
options.B: The initial evaluation focuses on cardiac disease severity, while psychosocial factors are reviewed later if problems arise after transplant listing.
options.C: The evaluation considers adherence and medical risk, but social support and mental-health factors mainly affect care after transplantation rather than candidacy.
options.D: The evaluation is completed primarily by the transplant physician, with nursing and psychosocial specialists involved after a final candidacy decision is made.

rationale: A is correct. The 2024 ISHLT guideline states that psychosocial evaluation is a key component of the multifaceted pre-transplant screening process and specifically identifies inadequate support, substance use, adherence, and mental-health concerns as factors relevant to post-transplant risk. The guideline also states that the complexity of medical and psychosocial issues makes a multidisciplinary approach paramount and lists, among others, a heart-failure cardiologist, cardiac surgeon, transplant nurse coordinator, transplant pharmacist, mental-health expert, social worker, dietitian, therapists, and palliative-care specialist. B is incorrect because psychosocial factors are part of pre-transplant evaluation rather than something deferred until after listing. C is incorrect because social support and mental-health assessment are explicitly part of candidacy evaluation. D is incorrect because the guideline describes multidisciplinary candidate evaluation rather than physician-only assessment followed by later team involvement.
educational_objective: Recognize heart-transplant candidacy evaluation as a multidisciplinary pre-transplant process that integrates medical assessment with psychosocial factors including support, adherence, substance use, and mental health.
source_organization: International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation (ISHLT)
source_document_title: International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation Guidelines for the Evaluation and Care of Cardiac Transplant Candidates—2024
source_version_date: Published August 8, 2024; current ISHLT professional guideline page rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: 2024 ISHLT guideline, Key Updates/summary page 5: psychosocial evaluation is a key component of the multifaceted pre-transplant screening process and identifies risk related to inadequate support, substance use, adherence, and mental health; the same summary states that a multidisciplinary approach is paramount and lists the transplant nurse coordinator among the relevant team members. Section 2.2 Psychosocial Evaluation; Section 2.2.2 Evaluation of Support, Adherence, and Mental Health, guideline page 43: recommends confirmation of social support, assessment of adherence and post-transplant regimen understanding, mental-health assessment, and use of psychosocial screening as part of a comprehensive multifaceted evaluation. Official ISHLT guideline page states the 2024 document replaces the 2006 and 2016 candidate-listing guidance.
source_claim_supported: Current ISHLT guidance defines cardiac-transplant candidate evaluation as multidisciplinary and includes psychosocial assessment before listing, with explicit attention to support, adherence, substance use, and mental health alongside medical factors.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team, Referrals, Case Management, and Continuity of Care: identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, assess referral/resource needs, act as liaison/coordinator of care, communicate significant information to other disciplines, and support continuity for clients requiring specialized care.
pdf_visual_verification: Relevant NCSBN 2026 Management of Care collaboration/referral content was visually verified earlier in this 2026-08-20 audit session. The official ISHLT 2024 guideline PDF was textually retrieved, but open/screenshot attempts on 2026-08-20 failed because the approximately 11.4-MB PDF exceeded the renderer's fetch limit; no visual verification of the ISHLT PDF is claimed.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'heart transplant candidate psychosocial support adherence substance use mental health multidisciplinary evaluation' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the candidate-evaluation item using the current 2024 ISHLT guideline alone rather than relying on the older 2018 psychosocial consensus statement. Removed the 'only' distractor and longest-key cue and replaced them with realistic errors involving delayed psychosocial assessment, post-transplant-only framing, and physician-dominant sequencing.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly reflects current ISHLT pre-transplant psychosocial domains and multidisciplinary candidate evaluation.
option_audit.B: Plausible sequencing error; incorrect because psychosocial assessment is part of pre-transplant screening rather than deferred until after listing.
option_audit.C: Plausible candidacy-versus-aftercare error; incorrect because support and mental-health factors are explicitly evaluated during candidacy assessment.
option_audit.D: Plausible physician-led workflow misconception; incorrect because ISHLT describes multidisciplinary candidate evaluation that includes nursing and psychosocial expertise before the candidacy decision.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four options contain comparable evaluation-process detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel explanations of the transplant-evaluation process.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after current ISHLT source-based reread.
